children: Wheat climbed nearly 2% toward $7.30 per bushel in mid-September, rebounding from a three-week low hit on September 18, as the latest round of US-China trade engagement fueled optimism ahead of the Trump-Xi summit.
Officials from both countries, led by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, met over the weekend.

Bessent described the discussions as “very successful,” while Lifeng said they were held in a “good atmosphere.” President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are set to meet in the US on September 24, with investors closely watching for signs of additional Chinese purchases of US agricultural products.
The Trump administration has said Beijing pledged to purchase at least $17 billion of US farm exports, on top of a separate commitment to purchase 25 million tons of US soybeans yearly.
Any further purchase commitments could therefore focus on other agricultural commodities, including wheat.

title: Wheat Climbs Nearly 2%
